Last Friday (21st), the ruling on the Hong Kong Alliance case was delivered. In the early hours of the morning, police took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle and removed her. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "sedition."

At around 5 a.m. last Friday, over 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a shirt with some seditious intent," and took her away in a police vehicle. When officers took the woman away, several officers kept directing reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and extended the orange cordon line towards Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, they put the cordon away. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reasons for the woman being taken away and whether an arrest had been made. The police replied this morning (24th) that a security operation was conducted in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts on 21 August, during which a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "sedition," and was detained for investigation.
